dedupe_keys.name: port environmental health risks review with the tarragona port industrial complex example

description: This review evaluates the health risks of living near ports and uses the Tarragona port-industrial complex in Catalonia as an illustrative example. José Domingo, Joaquim Rovira and Martí Nadal of Universitat Rovira i Virgili published it in Transportation Research Part D in 2026, using a structured literature search and a narrative synthesis organised from emission sources to exposure to impact. Ports handle about 80 percent of world trade and concentrate ships, cargo handling and logistics; the evidence consistently links port emissions with cardiovascular and respiratory mortality, asthma, lung cancer, adverse pregnancy outcomes and neurodevelopmental effects. At Tarragona, port and neighbouring petrochemical emissions together cause a quantified local burden of preventable deaths and disability-adjusted life years, although the port's share cannot be separated from the petrochemical complex and other urban sources. The authors recommend mandatory health impact assessment, health-based buffer zones, optimised freight routing and real-time air quality monitoring in port operations. Coverage: global literature and one Spanish port. Access: open-access article. Licence and cost: CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: a narrative review, not a new dataset; the Tarragona burden figures come from earlier studies. It helps set health impact and exposure parameters for port planning models. It relates to the THETIS-MRV shipping emissions data in the catalogue.
